This is a head-to-head comparison: gabapentin arm achieved a mean PUQE score of 6.35 vs metoclopramide's 13.22 (lower is better on this scale), with p=0.01. The metoclopramide arm is classified as 'failure' because it performed worse than gabapentin — the trial was designed as a superiority comparison of gabapentin vs metoclopramide, and gabapentin won. Metoclopramide's higher PUQE score (13.22 vs 6.35) indicates worse symptom control.

4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses were reported. The enrolled population (pregnant women with severe hyperemesis gravidarum) is appropriate for both mechanisms.

5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial is small (N=31), which is a notable limitation. Duration was only 1 week. No safety data was reported. The comparison is active-controlled (no placebo arm), which limits interpretation of absolute efficacy but is appropriate for this indication. The small sample size means results should be interpreted cautiously, though multiple endpoints converged on the same conclusion. The 'failure' classification for metoclopramide reflects its inferior performance relative to gabapentin in this head-to-head comparison, not an absolute lack of efficacy.
